summary: Jongcheol Lee specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and the University of Tokyo (PhD) under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992–1994) and the Academy of Korean Studies until 2001.

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He became Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies.
Joryu Chiba was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University until circa 1944 and later served there as a professor from circa 1968 to 1980.

Josef Kolmaš was a specialist in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at Charles University's Faculty of Arts from 1952 to 1957 and held a post at the Australian National University from circa 1967 to 1969.

Josef Schick worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber from circa 1880 to 1883 and held posts at Heidelberg University (1895–1897) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1897–1926).

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar who studied at Canterbury School, Dartmouth College, Columbia University, the University of Paris, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich. He held posts at Canterbury School (1933–1934) and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a Master of Arts at McGill University circa 2002–2004 under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College from circa 1945 to 1949 and served at the University of Minnesota from circa 1964 to 2000 as Professor Emeritus of geography.
Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University (~1961–1965) and trained under Anagarika Munindra and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Joseph Hackin worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied in Paris, including under Sylvain Lévi and Alfred Foucher, and served at Musée Guimet, the French Archeological Delegation to Afghanistan, and EPHE.

Joseph John Loizzo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and with Robert A. F. Thurman. He has held a post as Visiting Scholar of Religion at Columbia University.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University from circa 1947 to 1953. He held a long-term academic post at Temple University from circa 1968 until 2021.
Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington from circa 2010 to 2017 under the supervision of Richard Salomon.

Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Rikkyo University and the University of Chicago, where he later served as Dean of the Divinity School from circa 1951 to 1985.

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (circa 1978–2015), and held visiting professorships at United Theological College, UC Santa Barbara, and Bossey Ecumenical Institute.

Joseph T. O'Connell was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the College of the Holy Cross (~1958–1962) and held a post at the University of St. Michael's College from circa 1968 to 2005.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and held posts at INALCO, the Société Asiatique, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Northwestern University circa 1992–1997, studying under Adolf von Wuertenburg, Isshi Yamada, and David S. Pacini.
Joseph Wright was a linguist who studied at Heidelberg University from circa 1882 to 1885. He held a post at the University of Oxford starting in 1888.
Josho Nozawa was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi from circa 1930 to 1934 and served as a professor at Koyasan University.
